title: Finite Heisenberg Stone-von Neumann Property
body_html:
Finite Heisenberg Stone-von Neumann Property

Let $H(V)$ be the Heisenberg group attached to $V$, and let $Z$ be its center. For every nontrivial character $\xi$ of $Z$, there is a unique isomorphism class $\eta_\xi^V$ of irreducible representations of $H(V)$ whose restriction to $Z$ is given by $\xi$.

The degree of $\eta_\xi^V$ is $|V|$, and the character of any representation in this class is supported on $Z$.
proof_html:
Work with finite-dimensional complex representations, as in Finite Group Character Theory Basics. Let

$$ A=\{(x,0,z):x\in V,\ z\in k\}\subset H(V). $$

By Heisenberg Group Attached to a Finite Vector Space, \(A\) is an abelian subgroup containing \(Z\), and

$$ [H(V):A]=|V|,\qquad [H(V):Z]=|V|^2. $$

Define a character \(\widetilde\xi:A\to \mathbb C^\times\) by

$$ \widetilde\xi(x,0,z)=\xi(0,0,z). $$

This is a homomorphism because the multiplication on \(A\) is

$$ (x,0,z)(x',0,z')=(x+x',0,z+z') $$

by Heisenberg Group Attached to a Finite Vector Space. Thus \(\widetilde\xi\) extends \(\xi\) from \(Z\) to \(A\). Now set

$$ \eta=\operatorname{Ind}_A^{H(V)}\widetilde\xi. $$

By the induction statement in Finite Group Character Theory Basics, \(\eta\) restricts to \(\xi\) on \(Z\), and

$$ \deg(\eta)=[H(V):A]\deg(\widetilde\xi)=|V|. $$

We verify the hypothesis of Finite Heisenberg Central Character Criterion. Let

$$ h=(x,y,z)\in H(V)\setminus Z. $$

Then \((x,y)\neq(0,0)\). Since \(\xi\) is nontrivial, there exists \(u\in k\) such that

$$ \xi(0,0,u)\neq 1. $$

Set \(t=-u\). Consider the linear functional

$$ \lambda_{(x,y)}:V\times V^\vee\to k,\qquad (x',y')\mapsto y(x')-y'(x). $$

By Heisenberg Group Attached to a Finite Vector Space, this is the pairing

$$ \langle (x,y),(x',y')\rangle=y(x')-y'(x), $$

and that pairing is nondegenerate. Because \((x,y)\neq(0,0)\), the functional \(\lambda_{(x,y)}\) is nonzero, hence surjective onto the one-dimensional \(k\)-vector space \(k\). Therefore there exists \((x',y')\in V\times V^\vee\) with

$$ y(x')-y'(x)=t. $$

If we put \(h'=(x',y',0)\), then the commutator formula from Heisenberg Group Attached to a Finite Vector Space gives

$$ (h',h)=(0,0,y'(x)-y(x'))=(0,0,-t)=(0,0,u)\in Z, $$

so

$$ \xi\big((h',h)\big)=\xi(0,0,u)\neq 1. $$

Thus the hypothesis of Finite Heisenberg Central Character Criterion holds for \(H(V)\) and \(\xi\).

Now

$$ \deg(\eta)^2=|V|^2=[H(V):Z], $$

so Finite Heisenberg Central Character Criterion shows that \(\eta\) is irreducible. The same lemma also shows that its character is supported on \(Z\), and that any irreducible representation of \(H(V)\) whose restriction to \(Z\) is \(\xi\) is isomorphic to \(\eta\). Hence there is a unique isomorphism class with central character \(\xi\); denote it by \(\eta_\xi^V\). Its degree is \(|V|\), and the character of any representation in this class is supported on \(Z\). \(\square\)
